parts.t: Neighbourhood guide · Fraser Valley Regional District Electoral Area F, tagged Mission in MLS® · Hatzic Valley, FVRD Area F

Durieu is a sub-area name used in MLS® listings, and there is no boundary for it published by the Fraser Valley Regional District. The area belongs to the Fraser Valley Regional District, outside the City of Mission.

The FVRD’s Hatzic Valley Official Community Plan says the plan area is a portion of Electoral Area F, east of the District of Mission on the north side of the Fraser River, bounded by the District of Mission in the west, Hatzic Lake to the south, Durieu Ridge to the east and Stave Lake to the north. It includes the historic settlement areas of Hatzic Prairie, Durieu and McConnell Creek.
The FVRD’s Hatzic Lake Management Plan says Hatzic Prairie, Durieu and McConnell Creek are three farming communities at the north end of Hatzic Lake.

Written by Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®, Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, on October 18, 2026. I have worked in Lower Mainland real estate for 11+ years. Facts come from the official sources noted on this page. Rules and boundaries change, so confirm anything important with the Fraser Valley Regional District and Mission Public Schools (School District 75).

Planning, zoning and flood

blocks.text: Planning and flood notes for Durieu

parts.t: Plans, zoning and flood rules can be different for each lot.

The FVRD’s Hatzic Valley Official Community Plan says the plan area is a portion of Electoral Area F, east of the District of Mission on the north side of the Fraser River, bounded by the District of Mission in the west, Hatzic Lake to the south, Durieu Ridge to the east and Stave Lake to the north. It includes the historic settlement areas of Hatzic Prairie, Durieu and McConnell Creek.
The Hatzic Valley Official Community Plan (FVRD Bylaw No. 0999) was adopted on March 29, 2011, and replaced two earlier Dewdney-Alouette Regional District plan bylaws, 0454 and 0478.
The plan’s land use designations are Agricultural, Conservation Areas, Forest, Institutional, Limited Use, Local Commercial, Resort, Rural and Suburban Residential.

The plan says about 2,235 hectares of the plan area is in the Agricultural Land Reserve, a little over one third of the plan area and about 58% of the private land, and that about half of all private properties are at least partly in the ALR.

The plan says the southern part of Hatzic Valley, known as Hatzic Prairie, is largely within the Fraser River floodplain, which covers about one third of the plan area and reaches about 9.5 metres geodetic.

The plan says lands next to Stave Lake at the north end of the plan area are within the Stave Lake floodplain, and that BC Hydro and the Ministry of Environment have set the maximum controlled lake level plus freeboard at 83.3 metres geodetic.
The plan’s hazard section also covers geologic and stream hazards on the valley’s slopes and alluvial fans, where streams come off the mountain slopes.
The FVRD’s Hatzic Lake Management Plan (final December 8, 2020) covers Hatzic Lake and the catchment that includes the Durieu area at the north end of the lake.
The Hatzic Lake plan says Hatzic Prairie is susceptible to localized flooding.
Looking at the Central Fraser Valley route list from BC Transit, Mission has routes numbered 31, 32, 33, 34, 35 and 39, though none names Durieu.
